# Parse

Parses `input` into a value, rejecting duplicate names.

```rux
pub func Parse(allocator: Allocator, input: char8[..]) -> JsonValue ! JsonParseError
```

The default limits apply. A failure gives back the reason and its position and no value at all, so a document
that is not a document cannot be mistaken for one that is — which the old shape allowed, since it answered a
refused parse with `null`, and `null` is a document.
Fails with any case of [`JsonParseError`](/docs/api/json/json-parse-error), positioned at the byte where parsing stopped.

## Parameters

| Name        | Type        | Description                  |
| ----------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | where the value is built     |
| `input`     | `char8[..]` | the document, as UTF-8 bytes |

**Returns**: the document, or the failure that stopped it

## Related

<h3 id="duplicate-key-policy"><code>DuplicateKeyPolicy</code></h3>

```rux
pub enum DuplicateKeyPolicy: int32 {
    Reject = 0,
    KeepFirst = 1,
    KeepLast = 2,
    KeepAll = 3
}
```

What to do about an object containing the same name twice.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Json/Src/Parser.rux#L19)

**Cases**

| Name        | Value | Description                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Reject`    | `0`   | Refuse the document. The default, and the only policy that cannot be used to make two readers disagree. |
| `KeepFirst` | `1`   | Keep the first occurrence and discard the rest.                                                         |
| `KeepLast`  | `2`   | Keep the last occurrence, which is what most JavaScript-derived parsers do.                             |
| `KeepAll`   | `3`   | Keep every occurrence, in order. The document is preserved exactly, and lookup finds the first.         |

<h3 id="parse-with"><code>ParseWith</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseWith(allocator: Allocator, input: char8[..], limits: JsonLimits, duplicates: DuplicateKeyPolicy) -> JsonValue ! JsonParseError
```

Parses `input` under chosen limits and a chosen duplicate-name policy.
The long form of `Parse`, for a caller who needs something other than the defaults. The policy is a
parameter rather than a mutable setting on a shared parser, so two documents read under different policies
in the same program cannot influence one another.
Fails with any case of [`JsonParseError`](/docs/api/json/json-parse-error), positioned at the byte where parsing stopped. A limit that the document
exceeds arrives as `TooDeep` or `TooManyEntries` from the parser, or nested inside `Lexical` when it was the
lexer that measured it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Json/Src/Parser.rux#L644)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type                 | Description                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allocator`  | `Allocator`          | where the value is built                                |
| `input`      | `char8[..]`          | the document, as UTF-8 bytes                            |
| `limits`     | `JsonLimits`         | what to accept                                          |
| `duplicates` | `DuplicateKeyPolicy` | what to do about an object naming the same member twice |

**Returns**: the document, or the failure that stopped it
